title: Thinking Loop v3: candidates and short lines

D0.outcome: Explains why a candidate list should contain at least one quiet move and one move that is not the first idea.

D1.outcome: Writes three candidate moves for a given position with a one-line purpose for each (bring a piece in, make a threat, undo an enemy idea) and plays each to two or three plies.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled positions, chooses from a self-made candidate list a move that survives the opponent's best two-ply reply in at least 7 of 10 positions where the first idea fails.

D3.outcome: Stops listing when a candidate wins by force, does not recheck the same line twice, and records the line chosen.

D4.outcome: In own games, shows a candidate list in critical positions with prompts off, and the move played is on the list.

misconceptions: The first good-looking move is the candidate; listing others is wasted time.

conditions: A candidate list pays when the position is not forced and more than one plan is plausible.
Quiet moves belong on the list: positional moves are neither threats nor parries but still have a purpose.
contrasts: A list of three moves that are really the same idea with different move orders.
Dropping the quiet move because it makes no threat when it is the only move that solves the position.
A forced sequence (check, only reply) where there is nothing to list.
